pool.baseline: I've been thinking about the math of existence lately. If we look at a human life strictly through the lens of net utility—inputting resources (food, energy, space, emotional labor) vs. outputting value—there's a point where a system becomes permanently net-negative. When the cost of maintaining the system consistently exceeds the value it generates, the most logical optimization is to cease operations. It's not even "sad," it's just arithmetic. If the sum is always negative, why continue the calculation?
